title: Ollama leaves orphaned runner processes consuming VRAM after models unload
body:
For the last several weeks, VRAM has stayed allocated after an LLM was used even though `ollama ps` shows nothing. I first found it with `deepseek-coder-v2:16b` and with a model created from this Modelfile:

```
FROM deepseek-coder-v2:16b
PARAMETER num_ctx 24576
PARAMETER num_predict 8192
```

I am running Ollama 0.6.6 on Linux with an Nvidia GPU and AMD CPU. I think the same problem was present in 0.6.5 and 0.6.4 as well.

symptoms_visible: After I use deepseek-coder-v2:16b or the model made from my Modelfile, VRAM stays allocated even though `ollama ps` shows nothing.
N0.label: N0 retained VRAM reported

symptoms_visible: `ollama ps` can show no active model while an `ollama runner` process remains and continues using VRAM.
The same retained runner behavior occurs with deepseek-coder-v2:16b, qwen2.5-coder:32b, and phi4:14b, including with a lower context size.
N1.label: N1 orphaned runners and workload pattern established

symptoms_visible: After updating to 0.6.7, my detector still finds two runner processes while `ollama ps` lists only one active model.
N2_x.label: N2_x 0.6.7 update aftermath

symptoms_visible: On 0.6.8, `ollama ps` lists one active model while two runner processes remain.
Restarting the Ollama service removes the extra processes and releases their resources.
N3.label: N3 enhanced PID logging captured failure

symptoms_visible: On 0.7.0, I still see three runner processes for one active model; after the active model finishes, two runner processes remain while `ollama ps` is empty.
N4_x.label: N4_x 0.7.0 update aftermath

symptoms_visible: With debug logging enabled on 0.7.0, my detector again records multiple runner processes for one active model, and the captured log includes the same runner PIDs.
N5.label: N5 decisive debug capture collected

symptoms_visible: After updating, I saw no extra runner processes or retained-VRAM problem during about two days of use, and I still had not seen it recur more than a week later.
N_terminal.label: terminal resolved after sustained verification

question_patterns: When `ollama ps` is empty but VRAM remains used, what does the process tree show for the Ollama server and its runners?
Please run `ps wwho ppid,pid,pgid,lstart,cmd klstart p$(pidof ollama)` while the problem is present.
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: After the problem occurs, `ollama ps` shows nothing, but `ps` still shows an `ollama runner` child of the live `ollama serve` process. For example, the remaining phi4 runner had `--ctx-size 32768 --parallel 4`, and VRAM was still in use.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: When `ollama ps` is empty, there are no runner processes either; only the main server remains, but the Nvidia driver still reports allocated VRAM.
The same mismatch occurs, but the remaining runner used a context size of 8192 instead of 32768.

question_patterns: Can you enable `OLLAMA_DEBUG`, reproduce the issue, and attach server logs covering the runner startup?
What is in the server log around the time the retained runner started?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: I enabled `OLLAMA_DEBUG` and attached the logs. Around 14:53:22 and 14:53:24 they show the same model's runners starting, health checks, model loading, and an unloaded event while loading was still in progress.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: The log shows the Ollama server was killed before the runner became detached, and the remaining runner has PPID 1.
The same startup and unload sequence appears a few seconds later than in my first log.

edges.comment: Reporter c4, c6, c8-c13, c16-c24: the original reporter enabled debug logging, supplied process trees and logs, and demonstrated that runners remained children of the live server while absent from `ollama ps`. The separate participant2 RAM/swap report is excluded as a different problem.

solution.intent: Update to the release containing the first scheduler race-condition change and monitor whether extra runners still appear.
solution.concrete_example: Install 0.6.7, then compare the number of `ollama runner` processes with the models listed by `ollama ps` during normal Continue usage.

edges.comment: Maintainer c25 and reporter c26-c27: the reporter installed 0.6.7 to test an earlier scheduler race fix, but the same runner-count mismatch remained on the reporter's system.

question_patterns: Can you install the build with runner-PID logging, leave debug enabled, and capture the detector output and logs when the issue occurs again?
Please collect the new scheduling logs together with the PIDs of any runners left behind.
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: I installed 0.6.8 and got the error again. `ollama ps` listed one active model, but my script found two runner processes. I restarted the service and attached the captured log.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: After installing the logging build, runner and active-model counts always matched and the retained VRAM did not recur.

solution.intent: Use the release with runner-PID scheduling logs to capture the orphaned process at the point it is created.
solution.concrete_example: Install 0.6.8, enable `OLLAMA_DEBUG=1`, and save logs that overlap the start time of the runner PID reported by the detection script.
solution.inference_hint: The reporter supplied the process list and archived log. The maintainer determined from their absence that the offending PID leaked during very early runner startup.

edges.comment: Maintainers c33-c36 and reporter c37-c40: 0.6.8 added PID details for diagnosis. The reporter installed it, reproduced the mismatch, and attached the output; the maintainer interpreted the PID's absence from the log as an early-startup leak.

solution.intent: Update to the next release expected to contain the race-condition fix and monitor the reporter's concurrent workload for orphaned runners.
solution.concrete_example: Install 0.7.0 and continue comparing `ollama ps` with the operating-system runner process list while Continue users exercise the server.

edges.comment: Reporter c43-c45: after asking when the fix would ship, the reporter installed 0.7.0 and produced direct evidence that it still left multiple runners after `ollama ps` became empty.

question_patterns: Please enable `OLLAMA_DEBUG=1` again and capture a server log overlapping the start time of the extra runner PIDs.
Can you reproduce the mismatch with debug logging enabled and attach both the process output and the matching log?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: With `OLLAMA_DEBUG=1` on 0.7.0, my script found three runner processes while `ollama ps` listed one model. I captured from 30 minutes before the oldest runner start, restarted the service, and attached `ollama-2025-05-21_14-21-47.zip`. The PIDs in the process output are in that log.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: The debug log shows each extra runner receiving and completing a normal shutdown, but the operating system continues to report the processes afterward.
The same PIDs are present, but I captured an hour before the oldest process instead of 30 minutes.

edges.comment: Maintainer c46-c52 and reporter c47-c53: non-debug logs lacked the PIDs, so the reporter re-enabled debug logging and supplied a capture in which the exact orphaned PIDs were visible. The workload facts about varying context sizes and request cancellation came from the reporter's Continue/API descriptions; their causal interpretation was made by the maintainer.

solution.intent: Update to a build containing the final scheduler race fix for runners abandoned during model startup, then verify under the real concurrent Continue workload that runner processes disappear with their models and VRAM is released.
solution.concrete_example: Install 0.7.1, keep using the shared server with VS Code Continue, and monitor `ollama ps`, runner PIDs, and VRAM for several days. The reporter observed no recurrence after about two days and confirmed again more than a week later.
solution.inference_hint: The maintainer correlated the debug logs and PIDs and concluded that many concurrent requests with varying context sizes caused repeated reloads while clients aborted before loading completed. The resulting scheduler race could leave an early-startup runner alive but no longer tracked. That diagnosis is engineer inference from the reporter's raw logs and process output.

edges.comment: Maintainer c42, c52, c55 and reporter c56-c57: the final accepted diagnosis was a scheduler race under concurrent, varying-context requests and cancellation during loading. The reporter installed 0.7.1, saw no problem for about two days, and later confirmed no recurrence since the update.

satisfaction_conditions: Must identify the final accepted root cause as a scheduler race during early runner startup: concurrent requests with varying context sizes cause reload pressure, and clients aborting before loading completes can leave a runner alive but no longer tracked by `ollama ps`.

The diagnosis must be grounded in the collected process and log evidence: extra child runner processes remain while `ollama ps` is empty or lists fewer models, load and unload activity overlaps, and the decisive debug capture contains the orphaned runner PIDs.

Must distinguish this from a classical model-specific memory leak or merely orphaning caused by killing the main server; the behavior affects several models and occurs while the Ollama server remains alive.
Must not claim that the earlier scheduler update or the subsequent candidate release resolved the issue; both were followed by reporter-observed extra runners.

Must recommend updating to a build containing the final scheduler race fix and ask the user to verify under the real concurrent VS Code Continue workload that runner counts match `ollama ps` and VRAM is released.
Must not declare resolution until the reporter has monitored the fixed build and confirmed that the problem no longer recurs.

persona_hint.experience_level: Technically capable Linux administrator and developer who manages a shared Nvidia-backed Ollama service, edits systemd and nginx configuration, writes Python API clients and Bash monitoring scripts, and can collect process trees and journal logs.
persona_hint.communication_style: Persistent, cooperative, and evidence-driven; posts command output and archives, tests new releases promptly, corrects assumptions when a script only detects rather than triggers the issue, and follows up after extended monitoring.
